newsitem.title: IRAQ: Oil in Ceyhan enough for several days' export-Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Oil in Ceyhan enough for several days' export-Iraq.

text.p: Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said on Tuesday that Iraq had enough oil in storages at the Turkish terminal of Ceyhan to cover several days of exports.
"We will pump oil to Ceyhan...the crude in storages there is enough for several days for tanker loading," he said.

The oil minister said several deals to sell Iraqi crude oil to foreign firms were ready. "We started sending them last night to the United Nations and from the legal point of view these deals have to be discussed one minute after 0500 GMT," he said.

The United Nations gave Iraq clearance on Monday to start resuming limited exports of oil from 0501 GMT on Tuesday to allow it to raise funds to buy food, medicine and other humanitarian items for Iraqis suffering under the impact of U.N. sanctions imposed on Iraq after its invasion of Kuwait in 1990.

Rasheed said Iraq hoped to double the amount of oil it is allowed to ship to world markets after three months. "We have every hope that there should be an increase in oil exports... either by 50 percent or double the amount," he said.
He said under U.N. Security Council resolution 986, the secretary-general had the right to assess the humanitarian situation in Iraq and suggest an increase in limited exports.
Rasheed said he expected tankers to call at Iraqi terminal of Mina al-Bakr at the Gulf and Ceyhan on Turkey's Mediterranean coast within the coming three days to load Iraqi oil.
The minister said OPEC had made clear to Iraq on both ministerial and governmental levels that it would be ready to accommodate any amount of crude Iraq was allowed to export.
He also said Iraq, under a directive from President Saddam Hussein, was determined to pursue a "balanced and wise policy to preserve the stability of market and maintain prices".
